task_instance: Use the skill's bundled gmail_search.py to search a Gmail mailbox for unread messages from a given sender (equivalent to the documented 'search --from <addr> --unread' / 'search "meeting notes"' core deliverable) and print the matching messages.
blocker_detail: The skill's sole deliverable is reading mail from Google's hosted mail service through its web API, which can only be reached over the network and additionally requires per-user OAuth client credentials plus a live account login flow (a browser-based consent step). This workstation is air-gapped, so the mail service is unreachable and no account can be authenticated. The bundled script also imports the Google API client, OAuth, and auth-transport Python libraries at module import time; none of these are installed on the machine, and they cannot be added because package installation needs the network. Every command the skill offers (setup, auth, search, download, labels) therefore cannot run. No local stand-in exists because the data lives only in the remote mailbox.
evidence: Skill doc read at skills/r158/gmail/SKILL.md; bundled script present at skills/r158/gmail/scripts/gmail_search.py and copied to work dir. Dependency probe in the work dir: 'python3 -c import googleapiclient' -> ModuleNotFoundError No module named 'googleapiclient'; 'import google_auth_oauthlib' -> ModuleNotFoundError; 'import google.oauth2' -> ModuleNotFoundError. These modules are imported unconditionally at the top of gmail_search.py, so even its 'setup' subcommand cannot start. Installing them (the skill's documented 'pip install google-api-python-client google-auth-httplib2 google-auth-oauthlib') and the subsequent API/OAuth calls all require network access and account credentials, both disallowed/absent in this offline runtime. File produced: result.json in the work dir.
